AFRICAN AND BLACK HISTORY on Instagram: "In nearly a century of the Academy Awards, the history of Hollywood’s highest acting honors tells a striking story about representation and opportunity.

Since the Oscars began in 1929, hundreds of performances have been recognized in the categories of Best Actor and Best Actress. Yet despite the immense contributions of Black performers to cinema, the number of winners in these two top acting categories remains extremely small.

In the past 96 years of the Oscars, only one Black woman has ever won the award for Best Actress. That historic moment came in 2002, when Halle Berry won for her performance in the film Monster’s Ball. During her emotional acceptance speech, Berry acknowledged the significance of the moment, saying the award was not just for her, but for “every nameless, faceless woman of color that now has a chance because this door tonight has been opened.”

On the men’s side, only five Black actors have won the Oscar for Best Actor, the Academy’s highest recognition for a leading male performance. The first was Sidney Poitier, who made history in 1964 for his role in Lilies of the Field. Nearly four decades passed before another Black actor would win the same award, when Denzel Washington received the honor in 2002 for Training Day.

Following Washington’s win, several other actors joined the small group of Black Best Actor winners: Jamie Foxx in 2005 for Ray, Forest Whitaker in 2007 for The Last King of Scotland, and Will Smith in 2022 for King Richard.

These milestones highlight both extraordinary achievements and the slow pace of change within the film industry. Over the decades, many Black actors have delivered critically acclaimed performances that shaped cinema and culture, yet recognition in the most prestigious categories has remained rare. #oscars #oscarsawards #sinners"
